source: Illustrative ICAR / CIMMYT Wheat Weather Impact Framework

heavy_rain.headline: Crusting & Emergence Risk
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) may cause topsoil crusting and seed rot before full seedling emergence.
heavy_rain.advisory: Ensure surface channels allow drainage so seedlings do not remain submerged.

moderate_rain.headline: Optimal Seedbed Moisture
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) settles soil around seeds, aiding uniform germination.
moderate_rain.advisory: Good germination moisture. Hold supplementary irrigation.

light_rain.headline: Light Germination Moisture
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Gentle rain ({amount} mm) maintains topsoil moisture for young shoots.

dry_spell.headline: Seedbed Drying Risk
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Prolonged dry spell ({durationDays} days) can desiccate young sprouts before root anchoring.
dry_spell.advisory: Apply light light irrigation if top 5 cm soil has dried out completely.

heat.headline: Warm Germination Conditions
heat.summaryTemplate: Above-average temperature ({peakTemp}°C) speeds up coleoptile emergence.
heat.advisory: Monitor moisture to prevent fast surface evaporation.

cold.headline: Delayed Emergence
cold.summaryTemplate: Cold temperatures ({minTemp}°C) slow down seedling emergence rate.
cold.advisory: Emergence will resume as temperatures recover.

heavy_rain.headline: Root Zone Waterlogging Risk
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) saturates the shallow crown zone, inhibiting crown root proliferation.
heavy_rain.advisory: Clear drainage furrows and avoid any field operations.

moderate_rain.headline: Timely Crown Root Moisture
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) at CRI provides vital moisture for crown root formation, saving an irrigation cycle.
moderate_rain.advisory: Skip planned CRI irrigation; weather provides ideal root development moisture.

light_rain.headline: Beneficial Shallow Moisture
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) moistens the active 5-10 cm crown root zone.

dry_spell.headline: Crown Root Stress - Critical Stage
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Dry spell ({durationDays} days) at CRI restricts crown root anchoring, causing permanent tiller loss.
dry_spell.advisory: Apply CRI irrigation immediately. This is the single most sensitive moisture stage.

heat.headline: High Evapotranspiration at CRI
heat.summaryTemplate: Temperatures reaching {peakTemp}°C accelerate soil drying around crown roots.
heat.advisory: Check root depth moisture; irrigate if dry.

cold.headline: Mild Frost Tolerance
cold.summaryTemplate: Wheat at CRI is hardy to low temperatures ({minTemp}°C).

heavy_rain.headline: Waterlogging at Tillering
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) during tillering creates waterlogging, causing root asphyxiation and yellowing.
heavy_rain.advisory: Open field drains to prevent standing water for more than 24 hours. Hold nitrogen top-dressing.

moderate_rain.headline: Beneficial Tillering Moisture
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) fuels vigorous shoot growth and improves fertilizer uptake.
moderate_rain.advisory: Skip irrigation. Schedule nitrogen top-dressing right before or after the shower.

light_rain.headline: Good Vegetative Growth Moisture
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) supports canopy expansion.

dry_spell.headline: Tiller Abortion Risk
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Dry spell ({durationDays} days) forces the plant to abort secondary tillers, reducing earhead count.
dry_spell.advisory: Apply light irrigation to maintain tiller density.

cold.headline: Favorable Cool Tillering Weather
cold.summaryTemplate: Cool weather ({minTemp}°C) promotes healthy tiller branching and strong crown roots.

heavy_rain.headline: Lodging & Stem Weakness Risk
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) combined with wind risks early stem lodging and foliar disease.
heavy_rain.advisory: Ensure rapid drainage. Delay any chemical sprays until canopy dries.

moderate_rain.headline: Ear Development Moisture
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) supports rapid stem elongation and earhead development.

light_rain.headline: Favorable Canopy Moisture
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) sustains active jointing growth.

dry_spell.headline: Reduced Spikelet Count Risk
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Moisture deficit ({durationDays} dry days) restricts head size and potential grains per spike.
dry_spell.advisory: Provide critical booting irrigation before head emergence.

heat.headline: Accelerated Booting under Warmth
heat.summaryTemplate: High temperature ({peakTemp}°C) accelerates phenology, shortening the spikelet formation window.
heat.advisory: Maintain soil moisture to buffer canopy temperature.

cold.headline: Cold Shock at Jointing
cold.summaryTemplate: Near-freezing temperatures ({minTemp}°C) can damage the sensitive growing tip inside the stem.
cold.advisory: Light irrigation can help moderate ground frost risk.

heavy_rain.headline: Pollen Washout & Disease Outbreak
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) during flowering washes away pollen, causing floret sterility, head blight, and lodging.
heavy_rain.advisory: Prepare field drainage immediately. Skip all irrigation. Scout for Fusarium head blight after rain stops.

moderate_rain.headline: Pollination Disturbance Risk
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) increases relative humidity and may disrupt open anthesis.
moderate_rain.advisory: Hold fungicide/insecticide sprays until flowers dry to avoid wash-off and pollinator damage.

light_rain.headline: Humid Flowering Conditions
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) dampens canopy; monitor for rust or foliar disease.
light_rain.advisory: Avoid spraying during active morning flowering (8 AM - 12 PM).

dry_spell.headline: Severe Anthesis Moisture Stress
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Drought stress ({durationDays} dry days) at flowering leads to pollen sterility and dramatic yield reduction.
dry_spell.advisory: Irrigate immediately. Maintain 50-60% available soil water.

heat.headline: Terminal Heat - Floret Sterility Risk
heat.summaryTemplate: Temperatures exceeding {peakTemp}°C cause pollen desiccation, poor fertilization, and empty glumes.
heat.advisory: Apply light, frequent irrigation to create evaporative cooling in the microclimate. Consider potassium spray.

cold.headline: Frost Induced Head Sterility
cold.summaryTemplate: Frost or sub-4°C chill ({minTemp}°C) kills open wheat florets and damages developing ears.
cold.advisory: Apply light evening irrigation to release latent heat and protect against radiation frost.

heavy_rain.headline: Severe Lodging & Grain Shrivelling Risk
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) combined with heavy top-weight heads leads to severe lodging and root rot.
heavy_rain.advisory: Ensure drainage ditches are clear. Avoid nitrogen fertilization.

moderate_rain.headline: Grain Filling Moisture
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) keeps soil moist for starch synthesis, but prolongs fungal vulnerability.

light_rain.headline: Canopy Cooling Shower
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) cools the canopy during milk stage.

dry_spell.headline: Forced Premature Ripening
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Drought stress ({durationDays} dry days) cuts short the grain filling duration, reducing 1000-grain weight.
dry_spell.advisory: Apply final grain-filling irrigation before dough stage.

heat.headline: Terminal Heat - Shriveled Grain Risk
heat.summaryTemplate: Extreme temperature ({peakTemp}°C) halts starch synthase enzymes, leading to early forced maturity and light grains.
heat.advisory: Apply canopy misting/light irrigation. Consider foliar spray of potassium nitrate or thiourea.

cold.headline: Extended Grain Filling
cold.summaryTemplate: Cooler temperatures ({minTemp}°C) slow down starch translocation but may increase final grain size.

heavy_rain.headline: Pre-Harvest Sprouting & Direct Crop Loss
heavy_rain.summaryTemplate: Heavy rain ({amount} mm) on mature standing wheat triggers in-ear sprouting, fungal blackening, and severe lodging.
heavy_rain.advisory: Harvest mature crop immediately before the rain arrives if combine harvester is available, or secure drainage.

moderate_rain.headline: Harvest Delay & Grain Quality Degradation
moderate_rain.summaryTemplate: Moderate rain ({amount} mm) rewets dry grain, delaying harvest and degrading test weight and milling grade.
moderate_rain.advisory: Postpone harvest until 2 sunny days dry grain moisture below 14%.

light_rain.headline: Moisture Hindrance at Harvest
light_rain.summaryTemplate: Light rain ({amount} mm) increases straw dampness, preventing clean threshing.
light_rain.advisory: Wait for morning dew and moisture to dissipate before combining.

dry_spell.headline: Ideal Harvest Weather
dry_spell.summaryTemplate: Dry, sunny weather ({durationDays} dry days) allows rapid grain moisture drop to safe storage levels (<12%).
dry_spell.advisory: Excellent harvest window. Complete harvesting and threshing promptly.

heat.headline: Fast Desiccation for Harvest
heat.summaryTemplate: Warm dry conditions ({peakTemp}°C) accelerate final field dry-down.
heat.advisory: Prepare machinery and storage bins for harvesting.

cold.headline: Slow Grain Drying
cold.summaryTemplate: Cool damp air ({minTemp}°C) slows natural grain dry-down.
